incomplete_candidate.title: Crossed graphical component-preservation observation for an embedded height-family sign
incomplete_candidate.mechanism: A writer optionally combines a reusable bench-like motif with a reusable tall-body motif. Their visual co-presence is a physical construction claim; expanded source-letter identity is a separate stronger claim.
incomplete_candidate.distinguishing_prediction: Identify diagnostic bench and height-family features from free exemplars before examining fixed embedded targets. Predict both feature bundles in embedded forms; include a wrong-height-family distractor. Use predefined missing/uncertain outcomes, not free pixel deformation until every target fits. A shared fusion rule across a second withheld height family is more informative than inspecting one symbol already named cHh.
incomplete_candidate.smallest_selection_requirement: Root must identify an admitted source-bound set of free bench, free height, embedded target and contrasting height exemplar, ideally same hand/line. This bounded producer did not establish such a specimen packet and did not acquire images or query native strings to manufacture it.
incomplete_candidate.controls: Separate physical component identification from transcription labels; preserve wrong-component alternatives and whole-sign mimicry. No automated segmentation or template-fitting pipeline before specimen and discriminating-feature adequacy.
limitations: Static ink cannot determine stroke order, pen lifts, BH versus HB chronology or phoneme order.
A complex single letter can reuse graphical components; positive geometry does not prove two linguistic units or equal meanings between expanded/fused words.
Exact overlap/shared-stroke rule and feature scoring need a physically motivated contract before testing. Unspecified overlap allowance would make the claim unfalsifiable.
Not a proposal to retry old connected-arch vowel or gap conditions.
